title: Assessment 1: Baseline (Before SHINE Activities)

administration.sourceTimingNote: NOTE:  Administer before students use the gamification platform or begin the independent study.

instructions: INSTRUCTIONS: This assessment is a required activity for all students participating in the SHINE Project and it is also being used for research purposes by the SHINE Project leadership team (Drs. Esther Isabelle Wilder, Gregory Broberg, Eduardo Vianna, and Toni Watt). If you wish to be a participant in the SHINE Research Program, you must complete the Institutional Review Board (IRB) consent form prior to completing this assessment. Please complete this assessment on your own and in one sitting. It should take you approximately one hour to finish. Please try your best on every item.

sections.title: Attitudinal Questions
instructions: For each statement, select the response that best represents how you feel at this point. Use the same scale for every statement.

I feel confident using spreadsheet software to carry out simple data analysis.
I am comfortable calculating percentages.
I feel confident interpreting percentages.
I am comfortable working with ratios.
I feel confident reading bivariate tables that compare two variables.
I feel confident distinguishing between row percentages and column percentages in a table.
I feel confident identifying independent and dependent variables in a research question.

sections.title: Cognitive Questions
instructions: Select the best answer for each question. A calculator and spreadsheet software may be used for this portion of the assessment, but please do not use artificial intelligence to look up the answers. We use this assessment to evaluate the effectiveness of our program and to design instructional practices that best serve students, but not to evaluate individual students. Your performance on the assessment will not affect your standing in the SHINE Project.

questions.prompt: A researcher is interested in whether the amount of time college students spend working for pay is related to the amount of time they spend studying.  Which of the following is the best quantitative research question for the study?

options.label: A
options.text: How many college students work for pay and study?

options.label: B
options.text: How do students feel about working while attending college?

options.label: C
options.text: Is the number of hours students work for pay each week related to the number of hours they study each week?

options.label: D
options.text: Should college students work a certain number of hours while attending college?

questions.prompt: Which of the following would be an appropriate hypothesis if you are interested in whether the amount of time college students spend working for pay is related to the amount of time they spend studying?

options.label: C
options.text: Employment is an important issue for college students

options.label: D
options.text: Some students work and some students do not
